title: From Agent Behaviour to Agent-Friendly Documentation: An Empirical Study of How Coding Agents Discover, Read, and Write Technical Documentation
title_zh: 从智能体行为到智能体友好文档：编码智能体发现、阅读与编写技术文档的实证研究
abstract_en: Technical documentation is written for human developers, but an increasing share of software changes is now authored by autonomous coding agents. Which documents they consult, when, and what follows remain unknown. We conduct a behaviour-grounded study of agent-documentation interaction across two public datasets: 557 agentic coding sessions from SWE-chat, yielding 94,813 development events including 3,033 documentation interactions; and 33,097 agentic pull requests from AIDev, with 690,260 classified file-level change records. Four findings challenge current documentation practice. First, agents' documentation work is dominated by agent-facing artefacts: instruction files and working notes account for 60.5% of all documentation interactions, versus 10.6% for classical technical documentation and 1.3% for API references. Second, the link between consultation and code editing is unresolved: the adjacent transition probability is 0.002 and the unadjusted three-event lift 1.05, whereas a stage-adjusted model places it above unity (OR 1.33 [1.09, 1.62]); documentation creation is elevated unadjusted (lift 1.67) but its adjusted interval includes unity. Third, no explicit documentation-based validation sequence was observed, and consultation is associated with less immediate testing (lift 0.23, cluster CI 0.08-0.45; adjusted OR 0.39 [0.25, 0.60]). Fourth, consultation is self-initiated (70.2%) far more often than failure-driven (7.5%), and documentation trails code: among multi-commit pull requests changing both, code is touched first 4.7x more often. From these traces we derive a descriptive model of agent-documentation interaction as a two-lobed cycle rather than a linear journey, and show that two widely assumed properties of "agent-friendly" documentation - actionability and verifiability - lack consistent behavioural support. We release our pipeline, coding scheme, and event-level data.
abstract_zh: 技术文档通常面向人类开发者编写，但如今越来越多的软件变更由自主编码智能体完成，而它们会查阅哪些文档、何时查阅以及查阅后采取何种行动，仍缺乏系统认识。本文基于两个公开数据集开展行为驱动的智能体—文档交互研究：SWE-chat 中的 557 个智能体编码会话，包含 94,813 个开发事件和 3,033 次文档交互；以及 AIDev 中的 33,097 个智能体 Pull Request，包含 690,260 条分类后的文件级变更记录。研究得到四项挑战现有文档实践的发现。第一，智能体的文档活动主要围绕面向智能体的材料展开：指令文件和工作笔记占全部文档交互的 60.5%，传统技术文档仅占 10.6%，API 参考文档仅占 1.3%。第二，查阅文档与编辑代码之间的关系尚无定论：相邻转移概率仅为 0.002，未经调整的三事件提升度为 1.05；但控制开发阶段后，其发生比高于 1（OR 1.33，95% CI [1.09, 1.62]）。文档创建在未调整分析中有所增加（lift 1.67），但调整后的置信区间包含 1。第三，数据中没有观察到明确的“基于文档进行验证”序列，而且查阅文档与短期内更少执行测试相关（lift 0.23，聚类 CI [0.08, 0.45]；调整后 OR 0.39，95% CI [0.25, 0.60]）。第四，文档查阅更多由智能体主动发起（70.2%），而非由失败驱动（7.5%）；同时，文档变更通常滞后于代码变更：在同时修改代码和文档的多提交 Pull Request 中，代码先被修改的频率是文档的 4.7 倍。基于这些行为轨迹，作者提出一种双叶循环式的智能体—文档交互描述模型，而非传统的线性旅程模型，并指出“可操作性”和“可验证性”这两项广泛假设的智能体友好文档属性，尚未获得一致的行为证据支持。论文同时公开了分析流程、编码方案和事件级数据。
key_points_zh: 研究覆盖 SWE-chat 的 557 个编码会话与 AIDev 的 33,097 个智能体 Pull Request，形成大规模事件级实证分析。
智能体主要使用指令文件和工作笔记，两者占文档交互的 60.5%；传统技术文档和 API 参考分别仅占 10.6% 与 1.3%。
查阅文档是否会促进后续代码编辑仍无一致结论；控制开发阶段后呈正相关，但未调整统计量几乎无提升。
未观察到明确的文档驱动验证流程；查阅文档反而与更少的即时测试显著相关。
文档查阅多为主动发起，且文档更新通常滞后于代码；作者据此提出双叶循环模型，并质疑“可操作、可验证”即智能体友好的常见假设。

llm_assessment.comment: The released trace data and empirical model provide durable evidence about coding-agent documentation behavior, but do not introduce a new harness or improvement loop.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 公开的轨迹数据和实证模型为编码智能体的文档行为提供了持久证据，但未提出新的运行框架或改进闭环。
